source: opcodes.md §1.1 / 223-2589 p.53 (OP CODE / FUNCTION / ACCEPTABLE LENGTHS)
note: The ONLY 1410 op-code length table that includes the 1-character chained form; the CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.16 chart omits it. Sourcing lengths from anywhere else (e.g. the tier-2 ilentest inventory) Instruction-Checks every legal chained J. `N` is 'any (no operands)' and is carried as the string "any", which isa/table.ts encodes as the empty ANY_LENGTH array. Ops Y, P, Q, $ and = are absent because §1.1 does not list them; their lengths come from opcodes.md §2 and §9.

negatives.R and X have no chained 1-character form: A22-0526-3 p.96, A22-0530-1 Figure 1 p.4, 223-2589 p.53 — three independent sources. An emulator that accepts a chained R/X executes instructions the real 1411 rejects on the length check.
negatives.D and T reject 2, 7 and 11: SimH's 7010 accepts D/T at 1, 2, 6, 7, 11 and 12. The 1410 documents 1, 6, 12 only (opcodes.md §3.3).
negatives.a 1-character chained J is legal: opcodes.md §1.1 J = 1 or 7; A22-0526-3 p.96 'BRANCH UNCONDITIONALLY … L = 1 or 7'.
